units.translation: ⟦1⟧ after ⟦2⟧ is very harsh, and ⟦3⟧ is obvious (as in ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧, etc.); in ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧ the figure is the same as here, even if one writes ⟦8⟧.
what toil does the city toil
Somewhere there must be something that inspires fear and keeps the minds of men within bounds. Thus Athena at 698 ⟦1⟧, and Menelaus in Sophocles' Ajax 1084: ⟦2⟧.
and not to cast all fear out of the city
but let there stand for me also some timely fear
so that it may remain well for a long time

— 521 ff. is in thought identical with 699 ⟦1⟧; ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧ 9* are repeated. Corresponding to ⟦6⟧, from ⟦7⟧ one can make with Paley ⟦8⟧ or even more easily ⟦9⟧ (426 etc.); from this then follows ⟦10⟧, since anastrophe, if not with ⟦11⟧, is not unusual in Aeschylus (⟦12⟧ ⟦13⟧, ⟦14⟧ 541. 587, etc.), and just as little is ⟦15⟧ with accusative in a local sense (⟦16⟧ ⟦17⟧ ⟦18⟧⟦19⟧, etc.). Thus ⟦20⟧ (⟦21⟧) becomes nothing standing in the bright light, no manifest higher power (= ⟦22⟧, but stronger); the opposite is the fear of hidden powers; which, as one sees, is not sufficient. Since now ⟦23⟧ is harsh - lengthening of a short final syllable by an initial mute + liquid is very rare -, and the strophe shows two short syllables for - ⟦24⟧, I write (with Hermann) ⟦25⟧ (⟦26⟧) ⟦27⟧. The ⟦28⟧ is (Dindorf) like Homer B 289 ⟦29⟧.
for who of mortals, fearing nothing, is just
as for example young children and widowed women
